title: A static counterterm cannot restore an entire kernel after changing port delays
statement: Unequal port delays change the source off-diagonal spectral density to gamma*omega^2*exp(-i*tau*omega)/2 *[-1+(1+eta)*exp(-i*delta_tau*omega)]. For nonzero delta_tau on the continuous band it differs from the old density. No constant Hermitian hopping correction makes the entire off-axis self-energy identical to the old one. This does not exclude matching one frequency, reoptimized controls or another target kernel.

requires: Same compact-band old target self-energy and unequal delays in the specified spectral matrix, with gamma>0,1+eta>0,delta_tau!=0.
A constant Hermitian counterterm is the only allowed repair; exact equality on an open off-axis domain is the requested target.

body: The difference of compact-band self-energy Stieltjes transforms decays as1/z at large off-axis z. If adding a constant restored equality on an open analytic domain, analytic continuation and the large-z limit force that constant to zero. Equality then forces all moments of the matrix spectral-measure difference to vanish; polynomial density on the compact interval gives zero difference, contradicting the changed phase density. The argument concerns recovering the entire old transform with only a static counterterm, not every possible frequency-local calibration or dynamical compensation. The actual idealized chiral-waveguide reading already assumes signed couplings, equal delays, prescribed dispersion and no extra radiation. Source .0005 delay/1-percent crossing is an unacquired unretuned grid diagnostic, not a manufacturing tolerance or universal no-go.
